record.name: Ad Astra Sky Supply
record.description: Ad Astra Sky Supply is a defense sustainment startup focused on keeping aging military platforms ready: producing certified parts for ground, air and space systems, from prototypes to full-scale runs, and bringing legacy assets into the digital age with digital engineering. It has an alliance with Wichita State University's National Institute for Aviation Research (NIAR) to build a domestic supply chain spanning digital engineering, advanced manufacturing, testing and certification, and works with the DEVCOM Army Research Laboratory, with a cooperative R&D agreement planned. Sustainment accounts for about 70% of a weapon system's lifetime cost. A woman-owned, veteran-led company founded by CEO Caroline Canfield in Prairie Village, Kansas, it launched at the 2025 Paris Air Show.
record.source: Wichita State NIAR release (Aug 13 2025); company site, Sep 2026; buildlist (founding year)
record.insight: The Pentagon spends most of a weapon's lifetime cost keeping it running, and parts for old platforms are often out of production. Ad Astra is betting that digital engineering and certified domestic manufacturing can close that gap faster than the original suppliers. It's very early, so contract wins through NIAR and the Army lab will show whether the model works.

record.description: Vight is building a two-seat electric vertical-takeoff aircraft (eVTOL) for private, door-to-door flight, aimed first at rural property owners and flight schools rather than city air taxis. Founded in 2025 and based in the SF Bay Area; Not Boring's Packy McCormick is an angel investor.

Personal aircraft have been 'five years away' for a century, so the milestone to watch is the first two-seat vehicle flying with a person aboard.
